title: Pre-auth OS command injection in <model> web interface (ping diagnostic)
preconditions: Network-adjacent (LAN), pre-authentication, service on by default
description: The ping diagnostic handler passes the attacker-controlled `host` HTTP parameter into a shell command constructed with sprintf() and executed via the vendor doSystem() wrapper, without sanitizing shell metacharacters. An attacker on the local network can inject arbitrary OS commands executed as root.
repro_steps: Observe telnetd bound on port 9999 with a root shell (no authentication required)
impact: Full pre-auth root compromise of the device from the local network, enabling traffic interception, persistence, and pivoting to other LAN hosts. If exposed to WAN via remote management, exploitable remotely.
remediation: Validate/allowlist the `host` parameter (numeric IP / hostname charset only) before use; replace sprintf()+doSystem() with an execv()-style call that does not invoke a shell; drop privileges for the CGI handler.
discovery_method: Version-to-version binary diff (firmware v1 -> v2) flagged a silent hardening of this handler; the vulnerable path was confirmed in the earlier release via Ghidra and reproduced in QEMU emulation.
